_README.purpose: Every tunable number in the retrieval layer, in one file. Read by retrieve/structured.py, semantic.py and rank.py. Nothing in those modules hardcodes a weight.
_README.why_config_not_code: These numbers are the argument the project is making, so they have to be inspectable and changeable without editing logic. docs/ABLATION.md records what happens when they change; a weight buried in a function body cannot be swept.
_README.fusion_normalize_semantic: THE MOST IMPORTANT SETTING IN THIS FILE. The v2 proposal specified Final = 0.6*structured + 0.4*cosine. Applied literally that does almost nothing, because the two terms do not share a range. A structured score genuinely spans 0.0-1.0. Raw cosine from a bi-encoder on biomedical text does not -- related and unrelated trials both land around 0.75-0.92, so the semantic term contributes a spread of roughly 0.07 * 0.4 = 0.03 of the final score while structured contributes up to 0.6. The semantic layer would be in the codebase, in the diagram, and in the write-up, and would be changing essentially nothing about the rankings. Min-max normalising cosine WITHIN the candidate pool restores its full range so the weights mean what they say.
_README.fusion_mode: 'weighted' is the proposal's formula with the normalisation fix. 'rrf' is reciprocal rank fusion, which ignores score magnitudes entirely and combines ranks instead -- more robust when one pool has an outlier that dominates min-max normalisation. Both are implemented so they can be compared on real queries rather than argued about.
_README.tier_scores: A criterion matching in the intervention NAME is stronger evidence than the same criterion appearing in the brief summary. Flat boolean matching throws that away. Tiers are per criterion FAMILY because the field hierarchy differs: for a drug the authority order is name > otherNames > description > summary, while for an indication it is the structured conditions list > a hierarchy alias > free text.
_README.criterion_weights: Relative importance when averaging. A criterion the user did NOT specify is EXCLUDED from the average, never scored zero -- see structured.py. Scoring an unmentioned criterion as 0 drags every trial toward zero and does so unevenly depending on how many fields the question happened to mention, which makes scores incomparable between questions.
_README.candidate_pool_size: Target size for the structured stage. Deliberately large: the job at that stage is recall, and the semantic ranker needs a pool to rank. Finding 'the best 10' with keyword filters is what v1 did.
